result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.maximum_spanning_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the maximum spanning tree using Kruskal's algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23161-L23257){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.maximum_spanning_tree( weight_attr=None, return_subgraph=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A maximum spanning tree is a subset of edges that connects all nodes with the maximum total edge weight. Essentially finds the MST of the negated edge weights. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of edge attribute to use for weights. If `None` (default), uses the edge's weight field. If the attribute doesn't exist on an edge, defaults to `1.0`. [return_subgraph]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a new Graph containing only the spanning tree edges. If `False`, returns a list of edge IDs as strings. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph or list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either a new Graph with spanning tree edges or a list of edge ID strings, depending on the `return_subgraph=` parameter. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Same Kruskal pipeline as `minimum_spanning_tree()` with the weight comparator reversed (equivalently, running MST on $-w$), so cost is $O(E \log E)$ and correctness follows from the cut and cycle properties applied to the negated-weight matroid. The construction is a standard tool for extracting a network *backbone*: retain the strongest relationships in a social graph, the highest-throughput links in a communication network, or the most similar species in a hierarchical clustering. Behaves exactly like the minimum variant on disconnected input, yielding one maximum spanning tree per component. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this triangle, a spanning tree only needs 2 of the 3 edges, so the maximum spanning tree keeps the two heaviest ones and drops the lightest: ::: {#e82ee674 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(weighted=True) g.add_node("A") g.add_node("B") g.add_node("C") g.add_edge("A", "B", weight=1.0) g.add_edge("B", "C", weight=3.0) g.add_edge("C", "A", weight=2.0) max_st = g.maximum_spanning_tree() total = sum( e.weight for e in [max_st.get_edge(eid) for eid, _, _ in max_st.get_edges_as_tuples()] if e and e.weight is not None ) # Returns 5.0 (chooses the edges with weights 3.0 and 2.0, dropping 1.0) total ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 5.0 ``` ::: :::
